text: If you were hoping for a quick jump into fall sunshine, Monday is taking its time. It’s still cloudy and 54 with a north wind around 14 mph, and the afternoon should stay cool, topping out near 60. There may be brighter breaks toward late afternoon and evening, but I wouldn’t count on a full blue-sky turnaround. The models aren’t entirely of one mind about a stray shower, though the broader call is dry, so a light jacket matters more than an umbrella. On the lake, north winds around 15 to 20 knots are easing, with waves running 2 to 4 feet before settling down tonight. Expect a chilly, mostly cloudy evening, a low near 43, and patchy frost is possible away from the water. Tuesday is the payoff, sunny and near 64, with much calmer lake conditions. Plan waterfront time for late today only if you’re comfortable with the wind, and keep the heavier layers handy after sunset.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - Happy Monday! A bit of early morning fog and drizzle is possible to start Monday, but it should not be long-lived. As we head into Monday afternoon, clouds gradually thin out, giving way to bright sunshine by the late afternoon and evening. Temperatures stay on the cool side, with most spots only reaching the mid to upper 50s. Clear skies Monday night will set us up for a chilly, potentially frosty start to Tuesday, with overnight lows dipping into the 30s.
